text:
Situation: Propofol has been on the FDA drug shortage list since 2020-04-10 and remains listed as of 2026-10-21, a period of 78 months. Corvale General holds inventory from two manufacturers: 143.95 units of NDC 00409469924 (Pfizer Healthcare India) and 102.23 units of NDC 00069020910 (Pfizer Laboratories Div Pfizer Inc). Corvale Lakeside holds only 10 units of the 20 mL vial (5 days) and 17 units of the 50 mL vial (7.2 days). P&T has approved these two NDCs as interchangeable alternates.

Why (FDA record): FDA posted the propofol shortage on 2020-04-10. Inspection 1106244 at Pfizer Healthcare India Private Limited ended 2019-09-06 with an OAI classification; the classification letter is dated 2020-05-25. A Warning Letter was issued to the same plant on 2020-03-25.

Our position: Corvale General has sufficient stock to support an internal transfer while maintaining a two-week supply. Corvale Lakeside is critically low. Hikma and Sagent are not on the FDA shortage list today and represent viable purchase options. Alternate NDCs from Pfizer Laboratories and Hospira are already approved for substitution.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 35 units from Corvale General to Corvale Lakeside — requires pharmacy director approval of the transfer request.
2. Purchase propofol from Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. — requires buyer execution.
3. Purchase propofol from Sagent Pharmaceuticals — requires buyer execution.
4. Substitute with Propofol 10 mg/mL from Pfizer Laboratories Div Pfizer Inc (approved 2026-08-10 by Jordan Hale, PharmD) — requires pharmacist verification at dispensing.
5. Substitute with PROPOFOL 10 mg/mL from Hospira, Inc. (approved 2025-12-13 by Riley Brooks, PharmD) — requires pharmacist verification at dispensing.

Not recommended: No action; delaying will worsen the shortage at Corvale Lakeside.
